title: Throughput regression - continuous batching misconfig scratchpad
body:
Goal: capture commands tried, logs/error snippets, quick hypotheses and next steps for the throughput regression tied to continuous-batching config changes. Personal scratchpad—unpolished.

Background:
- Regression observed after config roll (2026-02-18) that adjusted continuous batching thresholds + kv-cache eviction policy.
- Symptoms: sustained drop in overall throughput for long-context workloads (~2-3x lower tokens/s under same load). Tail latency OK for small seqs, but average tokens/sec drops when many concurrent long-context requests present.
- Affected cluster: prod-dedicated-gpu-pool-4 (A100s), model: redwood/rwkv-7b-ish (custom fork, kv-cache enabled).

Timeline/notes:
- 2026-02-18 14:10 — rolled batching threshold change: min_batch_size from 4 -> 8, max_aggregation_window_ms from 25 -> 40 (PR #987).
- 2026-02-18 15:00 — noticed increase in queueing and lower measured throughput on dashboards. Canary rolled back same day -> small improv but not full.
- 2026-02-20 — started reproducing locally using loadgen/long-context config. Wrote this scratchpad.

Commands I ran (local repro / cluster probes):
- run loadgen with long-context profile (100 concurrent clients, seq_len=2048):
  ./tools/loadgen --concurrency 100 --seq 2048 --model rwkv-7b --host prod-dedicated-gpu-pool-4:443 --warmup 30 --duration 300

- top-level process snapshots (during repro):
  kubectl -n serving top pods --containers
  kubectl -n serving logs deploy/inference-runtime -c runtime --tail=200 | grep -E "batch|kv|evict|queue" -i

- capture CPU/GPU utilization (NVIDIA SMI snapshot):
  watch -n 1 nvidia-smi --format=csv --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm

Observed logs / snippets (copied raw):
- runtime log (2026-02-20T10:12:31Z):
  [warn] batching: holding requests for aggregation (current=7, min=8, window_ms=40)
  [info] kv-cache: hit_ratio=0.12 miss=0.88 entries=16384
  [debug] scheduler: flush triggered by window expiry (40ms) -> batch_size=7

- scheduler debug: multiple flush-by-window events with batch_size < min_batch_size, so min_batch_size not being achieved often due to staggered arrivals.

- strange eviction spam (short snippet):
  [error] kv-cache: eviction queue thrashing: evicting 512 entries every 50ms (source=adaptive-policy)
  [warn] kv-cache: insert latency spike: 12ms (target <1ms)

Metrics snapshots during load (approx):
- tokens_sec: baseline ~120k -> observed ~45k under regression
- avg_batch_size: baseline ~16 -> observed ~6-8
- kv_cache_hit: baseline ~0.65 -> observed ~0.12
- gpu_util: baseline ~75% -> observed ~30-40% (wasted cycles)

Quick hypotheses:
1) min_batch_size bump to 8 + longer window_ms means most flushes happen on window expiry with smaller-than-intended batches (because client arrival distribution is bursty), leading to more frequent kernel launches and lower batching efficiency. Explains avg_batch_size drop and tokens/sec decrease.
2) KV-cache eviction policy change (adaptive-policy) is causing high eviction churn under these workload patterns (long contexts + many concurrent clients), leading to frequent cache misses and recomputation of KV states. Eviction churn explains low hit ratio and insert latency spikes.
3) Combination effect: smaller actual batches + cache churn -> more overlapping KV builds and GC-like eviction work, increasing host overhead and reducing effective GPU utilization.
4) There might be a bug where min_batch_size isn't enforced if flush-by-window happens; scheduler sets batch target but flush occurs at expiry with whatever accumulated. (log line indicates flush by window -> batch_size=7 even though min=8)

Commands to validate hypotheses (todo/tried):
- Force smaller window, restore min_batch_size to 4, and re-run loadgen to see if throughput returns.
  (tried rollback of PR #987 partially but not full revert)

- Temporarily disable adaptive eviction: set kv_cache_policy=LRU-fixed and increase cache_size to 2x -> repro.

- Instrument scheduler to emit metrics: flush_reason (window|min_batch|manual), batch_target, batch_actual. Added temporary log lines in runtime PR debug branch.

- Run per-request latency trace with trace_id mapping to batch id to see overlap and kernel launch frequency.

What I tried so far and results:
- Quick rollback of min_batch_size to 4 (on canary subset) improved avg_batch_size from 6->10 and throughput from 45k->78k (not fully restored).
- Switching kv policy to LRU-fixed (cache_size unchanged) marginally improved hit_ratio 0.12->0.18 but insert latency still spiky.
- Increase cache_size 2x (on canary) improved hit_ratio -> 0.38 and throughput -> ~95k. GPU util increased to ~55%. Suggests cache size was underprovisioned for long-context workload.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does flush-by-window produce batch_size < min_batch_size? Is that intended (i.e., min applies only to hold-until-min but window expiry overrides)? Check scheduler semantics in code.
- Is adaptive eviction policy evicting entries aggressively on write storms? Need to inspect policy parameters (burst_threshold, grace_period).
- Could there be a race between eviction thread and insert path causing insert latency spikes? Need to add coarse-grained profiling (malloc/locks) around kv cache insert and eviction.
- Are clients sending keep-alive heartbeats that cause request arrival smoothing or jitter? Maybe client side changed in mobile SDK.

Next steps (concrete):
- [ ] Add metrics/logging patch to branch 'debug/scheduler-flush-reason' (done) and deploy to canary (small 10% pool). Capture flush_reason distribution.
- [ ] Revert min_batch_size change fully on a canary and test end-to-end. If throughput recovers, plan staged rollback.
- [ ] Deploy kv_cache size increase + switch to LRU-fixed on canary and measure—if good, roll to prod with telemetry flags.
- [ ] Add contention profiling around kv-cache insert/evict (perf/tcpdump not great, consider eBPF for syscalls).
- [ ] Coordinate with client SDK team to confirm arrival patterns didn't change (Lina).
- [ ] Add integration test in loadgen suite that simulates long-tail arrival distribution (exponential inter-arrival) to catch this during CI.

Notes to self (retrospective):
- Config changes that look small (min_batch_size 4->8) can have outsized systemic effects because they interact with arrival distribution and cache sizing. We should have a canary policy where config changes are validated with a set of workload profiles.
- Make sure scheduler invariant docs clearly state whether window expiry can override min_batch_size. If not, fix behavior.

References / tickets:
- JIRA-4321 (incident): throughput regression in prod-dedicated-gpu-pool-4
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 (batching/kv changes)
- Confluence draft: confluence/redwood/CB-incident-2026 (investigation notes)

Quick reproducible commands for next on-call:
- start canary load: ./tools/loadgen --concurrency 80 --seq 2048 --model rwkv-7b --host canary-pool-4:443 --duration 300
- gather scheduler metrics: kubectl -n serving logs deploy/inference-runtime -c runtime --since=10m | grep "flush_reason\|batch_actual\|batch_target"

If I forget later: prioritize revert of min_batch_size and increasing cache_size as the highest-impact low-risk change.

-- Priya
